# Fixture — `slice-map`

Data for the `slice-index.py html` page, and the check that renders it together with the Slice Atlas
page `/essentials:slice-map-html` writes. It is **data, not a project**: no sources, no build.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `sample-data.json` | A hand-written, synthetic two-context instance of the data contract in `commands/slice-map.md` §6 |
| `sample-data-cycle.json`, `sample-data-twin.json`, `sample-data-scale.json` | Generated by `scripts/slice-index.py map` from `tests/slice-index/`; pinned by `tests/scripts/test_slice_index.py` |
| `expected.json` | Machine-readable expectations per data file, read by `render-check.py` |
| `render-check.py` | Renders each data file in headless Chrome (`--dump-dom`) and asserts on the DOM with the stdlib `html.parser`; then the two Atlas pages (below) |
| `TEST-GUIDE.md` | The ground truth, including the rows only a person with a pointer can check |

The hand-written contexts (`orders`, `billing`) deliberately include things a healthy project would not
have — an aggregate written from two contexts, an event consumed by nobody's publisher, a cross-context
read with no `via:` — because a fixture holding only well-formed data cannot tell a correct renderer
from one that silently drops the awkward cases. They also carry one deliberately *healthy* shape: the
seven-node chain `PlaceOrder → orders.place_order → OrderPlaced → billing.payment_policy → IssueInvoice
→ billing.issue_invoice → InvoiceIssued`, which crosses a bounded context in the middle and fans out at
`OrderPlaced`.

## The Atlas pages

The Atlas page (`references/slice/atlas/`) is checked from two inputs, neither of which lives here:

| Page | Built from | How |
|---|---|---|
| `atlas-fixture` | `tests/fixtures/atlas/` — three contexts, two declared journeys, scenarios, one manifest that does not parse | as `/essentials:slice-map-html` builds it: `slice-source.py` twice, then `slice-index.py atlas` (needs `uv`, or a `python3` with `pyyaml`) |
| `atlas-sample` | `tests/fixtures/slice-atlas/sample.json` — hand-written data and layout that reach every shape the page draws, a diff included | the same inliner, `scripts/slice_atlas.py` `assemble` |

The Atlas lays nothing out in the browser, so these checks are about the page working at all: every
lens mounts from a deep link with no console error, the incomplete-map banner, the unparsed manifest
drawn as an error card, a dock click that focuses its target, a deep link that restores the view, a
stale id that toasts. A probe script, prepended to the harness's copy of each page and never to the page
itself, records the errors and performs the click. `TEST-GUIDE.md` § The Atlas pages lists each check.

## Running it

```bash
python3 tests/fixtures/slice-map/render-check.py                  # four data files, the Atlas pages, both unrendered traps
python3 tests/fixtures/slice-map/render-check.py --only atlas     # the Atlas pages only
python3 tests/fixtures/slice-map/render-check.py --keep /tmp/sm   # also keep the pages and DOM dumps
python3 tests/fixtures/slice-map/render-check.py path/to/map.json # any slice-map JSON, generic checks only
```

Stdlib Python and one Chrome binary — no Node. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a check failed, 2 harness error
(unreadable input, a placeholder line or the layout constants moved, the Atlas fixture page could not be
built), **3 SKIPPED — no Chrome, nothing checked**.

Chrome is looked up as `--chrome`, `$CHROME_BIN`, then `chrome-headless-shell`, `google-chrome`,
`google-chrome-stable`, `chromium`, `chromium-browser`, `chrome` on `PATH`. Prefer
`chrome-headless-shell`, the Chrome for Testing build made for `--dump-dom`: the five slice-map pages
check in under a second with it. The Atlas pages cost one browser start per load — 19 loads with five
lenses — so they take longer; their timing is not yet measured. A full Chrome in headless mode is the fallback, and it is unproven: in a
container without a session bus it stalled on a trivial page, so CI should install
`chrome-headless-shell` rather than rely on a runner's `google-chrome`. A page that does not return
within 60 s is retried once, then failed as a hang (G10).

After a change to either page or to the data contract, run this, then check the by-eye rows of
`TEST-GUIDE.md` in a browser. After a change to `scripts/slice-index.py`, regenerate the three
generated files with `uv run --script tests/scripts/test_slice_index.py --update-golden`, review the
diff, and run this again.
